cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: No Tie Stands
cards.instruction: Turn every even outcome into a formal rematch with a new rule and a consequence for losing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've split the dinner bill exactly. I'll settle the tie with one more round: loser pays the tip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why should anyone lose? We both paid fairly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fairly gives us a tie. I'll accept a result that separates us; give me a criterion we can score.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We both enjoyed it. Isn't that enough?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then rate your enjoyment from one to ten on a napkin. Fold it; we'll reveal together. The lower number pays the tip. I'll count even happiness properly before we leave.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 declares another round after equal payment, A3 insists on a separating criterion, A5 turns B4 mutual enjoyment into hidden numerical rating with tip penalty; authority formalizes the rematch.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 fair split causes A3 tie diagnosis; B4 enjoyment causes A5 scoring it on folded napkins and simultaneous reveal.

relationship.evidence: B2 questions need for a loser and B4 offers shared satisfaction, plausible diners wish to finish without competition.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 equality in enjoyment to create the very contest B hoped to avoid, with explicit changed rule and consequence.

specificity.evidence: A1 bill and tip, A5 napkin ratings make a concrete dinner tiebreak with no unexplained apology requirement.
